chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: Small bands, rough clubs and Martha Raye at the Five O'Clock Club
summary: With big bands dying he played dangerous joints, then spent summer 1953 with Martha Raye in Miami Beach and fixed her messed-up band books in Las Vegas.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So from Bop City, that would be 19 -- what, about mid-'50?
Where did you go from there?
Well, I went back -- let's see, I went back to the little band and I was working around. The big bands were starting to die then, you know. It was very -- I

played around some terrible joints. I had to step over a dead body in one joint to get out the back door. I mean I didn't know he was dead at the time. I thought he was drunk and asleep. I found out the next day he'd been shot there. And I finally wound up in -- it was out here. I worked out in California with the big band, doing some dates around locally, playing weekends and things like that. And then I went back to the little band after that. And after a couple of scenes, like I said, stepping over this guy, and some of the -- the first time I ever ran into problems about getting paid, you know, and I said this is not for me. I joined Martha Raye, down at the Five O'Clock Club in Miami Beach, in '53, early '53, and I was there all summer with her. It was a small band, but it was a lot of fun. I mean every night was New Years Eve, and it was a delightful experience, because she's a wonderful gal. And she went to Vegas out of there, and she asked me to go along, because her music was so screwed up. Most of the parts were missing, and everything was -- it was a case of like I was telling you about, musicians marking everything, and she wanted me to go to Vegas to rehearse the band and explain to them what happened with the music, because she couldn't explain it, with all the markings and everything there, which I did. And after I got her straightened out there was no place for me there. I didn't belong to the Vegas local, and I had a situation there where her husband thought I was making time with Martha, and it was a bad scene, you know, which
